item.title: On Pareto-Optimal Estimation-Information Limits-Achieving Distributions for Integrated Sensing and Communications
item.description: arXiv:2611.27022v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: ISAC systems enable simultaneous data transmission and environmental sensing using a common waveform. Characterizing their fundamental estimation-information performance limits is of core interest in information theory. In this paper, the achievable data rate for communications and the Miller-Chang-type CRB on sensing distortion are adopted as ISAC performance metrics, both of which are functionals of the ISAC waveform distribution. Our aim is to characterize the optimal input distributions across the entire CRB-rate Pareto boundary, corresponding to different sensing-communication tradeoff preferences. Three types of power constraint on input waveform are considered, namely, i) general power (GP), ii) maximum amplitude (MA), and iii) constant modulus (CM) constraints. Under these constraints, Pareto-optimal input distributions are shown to exhibit a common structural property: the directional component is uniformly distributed over the complex unit sphere; the power distribution is discrete (excluding the communication-optimal point under GP, where it follows a Gamma distribution induced by Gaussian inputs). We further investigate and characterize their Pareto-optimal sensing-communication preference dependent support structures. Finally, numerical algorithms are developed under GP and MA to trace their Pareto boundaries and determine corresponding optimal power distributions based on their respective support characteristics. From both analytical and numerical results, we conclude sensing prefers deterministic power while communication benefits from a richer distribution of power levels, thereby revealing the sensing-communication waveform uncertainty tradeoff in the fundamental power domain.
item.dc:creator: Zi-Jie Wang

item.title: Hybrid-Field Interference Suppression for Low-Complexity Uplink Channel Estimation
item.description: arXiv:2611.27185v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Uplink channel estimation can be severely degraded by hybrid-field interference, where strong near-field intra-site interference is coupled with far-field inter-site interference. Although a joint near-/far-field dictionary can capture this interference structure, it requires dense angle--distance matching that may incur high complexity and performance degradation. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a hybrid-field interference suppression framework for uplink channel estimation. First, we formulate a hybrid-field interference model and analyze its sparse reconstruction. Then, to avoid exhaustive near-field dictionary matching, we propose a low-complexity interference-parameter estimation method based on the angle--domain diffusion pattern of the dominant interference. Using the estimated parameters, the proposed parametric interference-nulling orthogonal matching pursuit (PIN-OMP) algorithm suppresses the dominant interference components and reconstructs the desired uplink channel from the interference-suppressed observation. Furthermore, a physical critical-distance bound is derived to characterize the feasible distance-inversion region, and a conditional hybrid Cram'er--Rao bound (HCRB) is established to quantify the desired channel reconstruction limit under a reconstructed interference basis. Finally, numerical results are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.
item.dc:creator: Zihan Zhou, Li Chen, Ang Chen, Weidong Wang, Changsheng You, Yunfei Chen

item.title: ECG-LabWAS: A Laboratory-Wide Association Study Using a Fine-Tuned Single-Lead Electrocardiogram Foundation Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.27221v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Laboratory testing guides clinical diagnosis but requires blood sampling and processing. The electrocardiogram (ECG) is fast and noninvasive and may carry information about laboratory abnormalities, yet most AI-ECG models target one test at a time using 12-lead recordings. We conducted an exploratory ECG laboratory-wide association study (ECG-LabWAS), fine-tuning an ECG foundation model pretrained on 10.8 million ECGs to screen 50 laboratory tests from single-lead waveforms alone. The model was developed in an emergency-department cohort (MC-MED; 31,826 patients) and applied unchanged to an independent hospital cohort (MIMIC-IV; 115,921 patients). Of 89 abnormality directions (low or high values of each test), 33 met the same screening criteria in both cohorts. Areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve in the two cohorts were 0.841 and 0.838 for elevated NT-proBNP, 0.769 and 0.740 for elevated cardiac troponin, 0.755 and 0.731 for elevated creatinine, and 0.713 and 0.710 for low potassium. Discrimination changed little when the ECG--laboratory matching window was widened from $\pm$1 to $\pm$24 hours. Model predictions reproduced the co-occurrence of observed abnormalities but were about twice as tightly coupled, largely along one shared component consistent with overall illness severity; low potassium, elevated NT-proBNP and troponin, and markers of renal function retained discrimination beyond that of correlated tests. In exploratory analyses, ECG-assisted versions of the modified Glasgow Prognostic Score and the systemic inflammatory response syndrome criteria were associated with in-hospital and one-year mortality. These results identify which laboratory abnormalities warrant analyte-specific study with single-lead ECG.
item.dc:creator: Wenhui Liu, Yujie Xiao, Gongzheng Tang, Jianwei Chen, Jun Li, Guangkun Nie, Deyun Zhang, Qinghao Zhao, Shenda Hong

item.title: PepDeTech: Anonymous Occupancy Monitoring on a Battery-Powered 2.3k-Zone dToF LiDAR Node with On-Chip Processing and Bluetooth LE Reporting
item.description: arXiv:2611.27304v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As populations grow, society is increasingly required to shift towards systems of shared resources, which allow space, energy and time to be optimised. Facilitating this transition depends on data: how many people are present, when and where. From such information, schedules can be organised more efficiently and resources allocated where they matter. At the same time, privacy concerns and energy consumption limit deployment: cameras are frequently unacceptable, while simpler sensors miss people and cannot provide the full picture. This paper presents PepDeTech, a compact, battery-powered occupancy node that combines a 54 x 42-zone direct Time-of-Flight (dToF) Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) (VL53L9CX) with a Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) System on Chip (SoC). Three deterministic algorithms, background subtraction, motion history and a track lifecycle, run on-chip and count the people simultaneously, providing real-time occupancy monitoring. No trained model is involved, and setup takes less than a minute. Over three scenarios, background subtraction reaches a per-frame +-1-person accuracy of 83.6 % (mean absolute error (MAE) 0.70 persons), tested with up to five people present. At a 30 s interval the node draws only 3.1 mW, lasting 60 d on a 1200 mA h cell. Several weeks of deployment on a single charge make the node usable as a survey instrument for facility management: a room can be characterised for a measurement campaign without cabling, network provisioning or a camera, and the resulting occupancy record is what ventilation, lighting, cleaning and space-allocation decisions are argued from, ultimately resulting in more efficient resource allocation.
item.dc:creator: Victor Luder, F\'elicien Ndozi, Michele Magno

item.title: From Pilots to Position: Experimental Near-Field Localization for ISAC
item.description: arXiv:2611.27503v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables wireless systems to reuse communication signals for environmental sensing, potentially reducing the need for dedicated sensing resources. However, the achievable localization accuracy of communication-centric waveforms under practical hardware constraints remains an important challenge. In this paper, we experimentally investigate near-field target localization using OFDM pilot signals in a distributed communication system. We consider both coherent and noncoherent localization approaches, exploiting multistatic propagation delays and time-difference-of-arrival (TDOA) information extracted from pilot-based channel estimates. A hardware setup comprising two transmitters and four receivers was developed and configured to operate at 3.4 GHz with 198 MHz occupied bandwidth to evaluate localization performance under realistic propagation and synchronization conditions. Experimental results across 16 static target positions demonstrate mean localization errors of 19.8 cm and 18.8 cm for coherent backprojection and noncoherent delay-TDOA fusion, respectively. Furthermore, we investigate the impact of occupied bandwidth on localization accuracy of the two proposed algorithms. These findings provide experimental insights into the capabilities and practical limitations of OFDM pilot-based sensing, supporting resource-efficient localization in future ISAC systems.
item.dc:creator: Yunxin Li, Emiel Vanspranghels, Jialun Kou, Georgios Mystriotis, Achiel Colpaert, Rodney Martinez Alonso, Sofie Pollin

item.title: Geometrical Estimation of Electromagnetic Degrees of Freedom in Reflecting Environments
item.description: arXiv:2611.27615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The number of spatial degrees of freedom (NDoF) of electromagnetic communication channels in reflecting environments is investigated using a full-vector formulation based on dyadic Green's functions and equivalent electric and magnetic surface currents. The channel correlation eigenproblem characterizes the electromagnetic communication modes and their coupling strengths, while the leading-order NDoF is estimated geometrically from the receiver-accessible phase space volume in the electrically large regime. By combining two geometrical projection Jacobians, the phase space volume is related to the mutual shadow area, establishing the equivalence between the two geometrical NDoF formulations and yielding a two-polarization estimate equal to twice the mutual shadow area divided by the squared wavelength. The free-space mutual shadow formulation is extended to perfect electric conductor (PEC) reflecting environments through image construction and phase space ray tracing, accounting for specular reflections and geometrical visibility constraints. The formulation is validated against the eigenvalue spectra of full-vector electromagnetic channels involving planar PEC reflectors, a parabolic reflector, a parallel-plate waveguide, and a non-line-of-sight L-shaped corridor. The geometrical predictions agree with the observed spectral transitions across configurations involving multiple reflections, focusing, and blockage.
item.dc:creator: Yanwen Chen, Stefano Maci, Mats Gustafsson

item.title: A Dual-Mode Protocol for Space-Time-Coding Metasurfaces in OFDM ISAC Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.27813v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) frameworks assisted by space-time-coding metasurfaces (STCMs) rely on idealized surface models, which neglect the frequency-selective and angle-dependent response of the meta-atoms, and are typically limited to narrowband single-carrier communications. This paper addresses these limitations by developing a physics-based signal-processing framework for STCM-assisted ISAC systems employing wideband orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) waveforms, which accounts also for beam squint effects across the STCM aperture. On this basis, we propose a dual-mode protocol, in which the STCM operates as a time-varying surface during a short acquisition phase and as a conventional reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) during data transmission. In the acquisition phase, the angle of arrival (AoA) and the composite channel are jointly estimated by maximum likelihood from a single pilot OFDM symbol transmitted over a subset of active subcarriers, together with deliberately introduced virtual carriers; these estimates are then used to configure the RIS for data transmission. Numerical results validate the considered framework and quantify the gains achievable by the proposed dual-mode protocol.
item.dc:creator: Donatella Darsena, Ivan Iudice, Giacinto Gelli, Vincenzo Galdi

item.title: A Spatial Clustering and Resource Allocation Approach for Critical Services in Massive MIMO-Enabled Cellular Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.27832v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we address the challenge of providing quality-of-service (QoS) guarantees for critical real-time services in cellular networks where both real-time and non-real-time applications must be supported. Leveraging the spatial multiplexing capabilities of Massive Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) technology, we propose a joint clustering and resource allocation framework that limits network interference and enhances the ability to meet the QoS requirements of real-time services while still serving other applications. Our approach begins by clustering active users according to the direction of their channel vectors. Specifically, a downlink probing strategy is employed to group users whose channels lie in the same direction. Channel estimation and the derivation of the corresponding signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) are then performed based on this clustering. Subsequently, we formulate a resource allocation optimization problem across the user groups to satisfy the required QoS for critical real-time services while accommodating the remaining users. We rigorously prove that, in general, finding the global optimum of the resource allocation problem is NP-hard, and for a special case of the formulated problem, we establish a polynomial-time solvable algorithm based on linear programming. We then propose a suboptimal solution for the general problem using a linear relaxation technique. Simulation results are provided to confirm the effectiveness of our proposed approaches.
item.dc:creator: Eva Al Hajj Sleiman, Youssef Hussein, Vincent Angilella, Mohamad Assaad, Hikmet Sari

item.title: FR3-Band Capacitive-Piezoelectric Thin-Film LN Resonator for Heterogeneous Integration
item.description: arXiv:2611.27885v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This letter presents a capacitively coupled piezoelectric lateral-field-excited bulk acoustic wave resonator (XBAR) in single-crystal lithium niobate (LN) for frequency range 3 (FR3, 7.125-24.25 GHz). We develop a platform that simultaneously maintains high electromechanical efficiency (\(k_t^2\)) and quality factor (\(Q\)) while alleviating challenges associated with parasitic galvanic interconnections and is fit for heterogeneous integration above integrated circuits. A 100 nm air gap excites the second-order symmetric Lamb wave (S2) mode in a 500 nm thick periodically poled piezoelectric film (P3F) LN from a fused silica substrate via flip-chip bonding, yielding a resonance frequency (\(f_s\)) of 7.16 GHz with an extracted \(k_t^2\) of 12.25\% and \(Q\) of 100, facilitating a high \(Q\cdot k_t^2\cdot f_s\) product of 87.71. The results demonstrate strong piezoelectric transduction through a nanoscale air gap, supporting further development of the platform for heterogeneous integration of compact, low-loss microwave components.
item.dc:creator: Vakhtang Chulukhadze, Jiajun Huang, Marco Galli, Tzu-Hsuan Hsu, Udit Rawat, Yao Yu, Siddhartha Ghosh, Bichoy Bahr, Ruochen Lu

item.title: DNN-Assisted Deterministic Policy Learning for Adaptive IRS-NOMA-OWC Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.26742v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) has been considered a promising technology in optical wireless communication (OWC) networks due to its potential to overcome the line-of-sight (LoS) blockage issue and enhance coverage. In this paper, a dynamic IRS-assisted indoor non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-OWC network is modeled, and an optimization problem is formulated to maximize the sum rate subject to the quality-of-service (QoS) requirements of multiple mobile users, by jointly optimizing the power allocation and the IRS mirror orientations, from which the user's decoding order is induced rather than being fixed. Since the problem is non-convex and the channel conditions vary with user mobility, conventional optimization methods may incur considerable computational overhead. Therefore, a two-stage deep neural network-deep reinforcement learning (DNN-DRL) framework is proposed. In the first stage, the DNN estimates the user's positions and orientations in real time, removing the need for perfect knowledge of the user state. In the second stage, a deterministic policy gradient (DPG)-based DRL algorithm uses these estimates to jointly optimize the power allocation and IRS mirror orientations, with the decoding order updated according to the resulting effective channel gains. The results show that the proposed framework approaches the performance upper bounds and outperforms standard DRL algorithms, conventional optimization methods, and deployments without IRS in terms of sum rate and fairness, while achieving faster convergence. Furthermore, online adaptation of the decoding order maintains higher QoS satisfaction than a fixed decoding order, particularly under high user mobility.
item.dc:creator: Ahrar N. Hamad, Ahmad A. Qidan, Taisir E. H. El-Gorashi, Jaafar M. H. Elmirghani

item.title: Graph-XGB: A Hybrid GNN Framework for Outdoor-to-Indoor 5G Signal Reconstruction via Aerial-Only UAV RF Sensing
item.description: arXiv:2611.26828v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Delivering robust In-Building Coverage (IBC) is critically impeded by severe Outdoor-to-Indoor (O2I) attenuation, a constraint that intensifies as deployments move from 5G mid-band towards mmWave and prospective 6G sub-THz carriers, where losses of 60-80 dB have been reported across modern building envelopes. While Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) offer scalable exterior RF sensing platforms, a fundamental inversion problem persists: interior 3D signal states cannot be directly sampled from constrained exterior flight paths. This paper proposes Graph-XGB, a hybrid inference framework that decouples spatial topology reasoning from non-linear signal regression to resolve this challenge. A modified SpiderGNN encoder, operating on a topology-aware graph constructed with a physically grounded Floor-Aware 3D Distance metric and Bridge Edge Guarantees, propagates UAV boundary measurements into 128-dimensional indoor embeddings. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) compresses these into a 10-dimensional manifold retaining 96.6% of embedding variance, fused with raw spatial features and decoded by independent, physics-tailored XGBoost regressors. This decoupling mitigates the optimization conflict between smoothly decaying path-loss signals and volatile interference-dependent metrics. Evaluated on a real-world 5G NR dataset of 613 verified nodes spanning the 10 floors of a single building, Graph-XGB attains the strongest accuracy among the architectures compared, with $R^2$ of 0.759 (RSSI) and 0.770 (RSRP), improvements of 35.5% and 64.9% over the SimpleGNN baseline, using no interior RF measurement as a model input; indoor observations enter only as training supervision, with evaluation on held-out internal nodes. Interference-dependent targets (RSRQ, SNR and CQI) remain bounded well below the path-loss metrics, delimiting the reach of purely spatial inference.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: BESC 2026, Lecture Notes in Computer Science 17175, pp. 18-37, Springer (2027)
item.dc:creator: David Hason Rudd, Eunkwang Shin, Nithiwat Pattrapong, Huan Huo, Xiangmeng Wang

item.title: Self-Supervised Learning with Recursive Quadrature Filters for Neural Time Series
item.description: arXiv:2611.26856v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop self-supervised methods for training Recursive Quadrature Filter (RQF) encoders on unlabeled time series. RQFs are biologically motivated, complex-valued temporal filters that form a special class of diagonal state-space models (SSMs). Each RQF acts as a band-pass filter whose selectivity is determined by two learnable parameters: its tuning frequency and bandwidth. We separately introduce a self-supervised learning objective based on prediction error; the encoder is trained so that its current state predicts its own future activity. In the windowed mode, the summary of the current window predicts the summary of a later window; in the dense mode, the state at the current timestep predicts future log-power. Each RQF encoder is pretrained on a dataset and then a readout (e.g., a task-specific classifier) is trained on the output of the RQF encoder, with the encoder either frozen or fully fine-tuned. For multichannel EEG and intracranial recordings, a shared encoder processes each channel separately, and a spatial readout combines the channel representations using electrode locations. Across four neural benchmarks using scalp or intracranial EEG, the pretrained RQF system performs close to the state of the art while using a small fraction of the parameters of the competing models. For example, a 110k-parameter RQF system achieves 0.9247 +/- 0.0022 test AUROC on 100-s TUAB segments, above SAMBA (0.9054) at the same context with 9 times as many parameters, and 0.9040 +/- 0.0019 on 10-s segments, comparable to EEG foundation models with 3.2M-369M parameters.
item.dc:creator: Mirko Morello, Shivang Rawat, David J. Heeger

item.title: Dual-Agent DRL based Cooperative Beamforming and Trajectory Optimization for UAV-ISAC Networks
item.description: arXiv:2611.27346v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper considers a low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) network, where multiple ground base stations (BSs) provide integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) services for multiple communication UAVs (C-UAVs) and sensing UAVs (S-UAVs). With the objective of maximizing the average sum rate of C-UAVs over the entire flight episode, we jointly optimize the multi-BS multi-UAV ISAC beamforming and trajectory design, subject to the BS transmit power budget and the sensing signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) constraints of S-UAVs, as well as the flight mission and collision avoidance constraints of C-UAVs and S-UAVs. Based on the multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL) technique, we develop a dual-agent scheme, termed DeepDA-OPT, to solve the resulting constrained Markov decision process (MDP). In the proposed DeepDA-OPT scheme, two agents, i.e., Agent-B and Agent-T, are specifically deployed for learning the multi-BS ISAC transmit beamformers and the C-UAV/S-UAV trajectories, respectively, where the optimal BS receive beamformers for the sensing echo signals of S-UAVs are obtained in closed form by leveraging the generalized Rayleigh quotient theorem. To mitigate the overestimation of value functions, both Agent-B and Agent-T are trained based on the twin-delayed deep deterministic (TD3) policy-gradient algorithm. In addition, a constraint-aware noise exploration policy is employed, and the reward function is designed to incorporate a sensing penalty and a flight urgency penalty, thereby guiding the training of Agent-B and Agent-T. Numerical results show that, compared with the baseline schemes, the proposed DeepDA-OPT scheme achieves a higher average sum rate of C-UAVs, while the sensing SINR constraints are empirically well satisfied and no collision violation is observed under the evaluated settings.
item.dc:creator: Kaijian Yang, Feng Wang, Guojun Han, Xin Wang, Vincent K. N. Lau

item.title: TITAN: DRL-Based Dynamic Scheduling and Resource Allocation for Tactile Internet
item.description: arXiv:2611.27560v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tactile Internet (TI) applications require ultra-reliable, low-latency tactile communication alongside video traffic. However, tactile Quality of Service (QoS) requirements vary with the interaction context, making fixed resource allocation inefficient. In this paper, we propose TITAN (Two-Timescale Integrated Tactile Internet over 5G Access Networks), a dynamic scheduling and resource allocation (SRA) scheme. TITAN receives time-varying tactile QoS profiles from a higher-layer module and adapts SRA to the current QoS profile and network state. A deep reinforcement learning-based agent splits the available network bandwidth between tactile and video streams at a slow timescale, while a fast-timescale scheduler allocates resource blocks among active user equipment. Through simulations, we show that TITAN simultaneously satisfies both tactile and video QoS targets and achieves a performance gain of 7.64 percentage points (pp) in the joint satisfaction rate over the best-performing static SRA baseline.
item.dc:creator: Qingrui Fan, Vineet Gokhale, Jayakrishnan Nair, Johannes Cottyn

item.title: Passivity Correction of the Thermistor Model in Bolometric Power Sensors and Its Dependence on Bead Temperature
item.description: arXiv:2611.27744v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper closes a series of works on thermistor bolometric power sensors, coaxial and waveguide, by treating what the two have in common. The per-state transformation m introduced in the waveguide work, which corrects the thermistor impedances of the model in each bridge state so that the two-port of the mount is passive, is analyzed on the eleven sensors of the preceding papers: the corrections are a few tenths of a percent in the coaxial mounts and one to two percent in the waveguide mounts, follow one pattern within each family, and the hottest state is the one whose efficiency departs most from the others. The transformation is tested by an independent measurement: the substituted powers of the three states, read with the manufacturer's procedure against a leveled source whose reflection is obtained from the closure of three Apollonius circles, give efficiency ratios of 0.999 +/- 0.016 and 0.997 +/- 0.008 (k = 2), which contain the values at the passivity floor (0.996, 0.998) and exclude those of the first pass (0.941, 1.023). Three sensors were swept in the bridge resistance, 23 and 31 states, and a fourth is treated apart: the correction reduces to one constant per state, the parallel resistance of the bead, represented by a law with one term scaling with the bridge resistance and one exponential in the bead temperature, with one thermal coefficient per family. The same property explains why the cross-ratio of four measured reflection coefficients, invariant under any state-independent two-port, departs from that of the four bridge resistances.
item.dc:creator: Patricio Greco

item.title: A Microwave-Photonics Formulation of the Rydberg-Atom Receiver
item.description: arXiv:2611.27942v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The performance of Rydberg-atom receivers is seldom stated as a radio-frequency (RF) link budget. The receiver is shown to be an intensity-modulated direct-detection analog optical link whose modulator is the laser-driven vapor. The transmission of a warm vapor is derived in closed form by averaging the four-level response over atomic velocities. The conversion gain, noise figure, bandwidth, intercept points, and spurious-free dynamic range follow from this one function. For a weak probe the instantaneous bandwidth is half the width of the transparency window in two-photon detuning. The local-oscillator beat places the second-order intercept near twice the local-oscillator field, so the local oscillator sets the even-order linearity. For a rubidium transition at 17.04 GHz the closed forms agree with a velocity-resolved density-matrix model to 1% for the slope and the intercepts and to 10% for the bandwidth. They underestimate the group delay by a third. The response is tied to atomic constants, and the sensing volume escapes the Chu limit. However, the noise figure of a warm vapor rules it out as a general replacement for an antenna and low-noise amplifier.
item.dc:creator: David Rosser

item.title: On the Complete Feature Set for ADHD Classification in Children and Adolescents Based on EEG Signals
item.description: arXiv:2611.27970v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is a neurodevelopmental condition that can affect attention, activity and impulse control. Electroencephalography (EEG) records brain activity as children and adolescents perform cognitive tasks. However, comparing features derived from these recordings requires consistent signal preparation, shared analysis windows and documented quality decisions. We curated 669 existing BALLADEER recordings from 156 participants across five task conditions so that researchers can compare seven EEG feature families on the same time intervals for each participant and task. The dataset links continuous signals to precomputed measurements from 115 feature definitions or templates and records the quality decisions made for each recording. Analyses must still account for repeated measurements within participants, residual artefacts and differences between acquisition systems. Technical validation covered signal integrity, numerical checks on feature estimators and completeness of the released files. In every task, the median proportion of recording time retained after preprocessing was 100%. To illustrate reuse, we report saved participant-held-out evaluations comparing XGBoost using all seven families on eight-second windows with a predictor based only on recruitment-group prevalence in the training fold. Recruitment-group discrimination was stronger in Robots than in the three Slackline conditions. These descriptive results from overlapping cohorts do not establish diagnostic validity. The dataset, curation software and aggregate results for the predictive example are publicly available.
item.dc:creator: Javier Sanchis, \'Alvaro Navarro, Jorge Garc\'ia-Carrasco, Tahar Kechadi, Juan Trujillo

item.title: UNILocPro: Unified Localization Integrating Model-Based Geometry and Channel Charting
item.description: arXiv:2510.27394v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we propose a unified framework (called UNILocPro) that integrates model-based geometry and channel charting (CC) for localization via a single massive multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) base station (BS) in mixed line-of-sight (LoS)/non-line-of-sight (NLoS) scenarios. Specifically, based on LoS/NLoS identification, an adaptive activation between the model-based and CC-based methods is conducted. Aiming for unsupervised learning, information obtained from the model-based method is utilized to train the CC model, where a pairwise distance loss (involving a new dissimilarity metric design), a triplet loss (if timestamps are available), a LoS-based loss, and an optimal transport (OT)-based loss are jointly employed such that the global geometry can be well preserved. To reduce the training complexity, we propose a low-complexity implementation (called UNILoc), where the CC model is trained with self-generated labels produced by a single pre-training OT transformation, which avoids iterative Sinkhorn updates involved in the OT-based loss computation. Extensive numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed unified frameworks achieve significantly improved positioning accuracy compared to both model-based and CC-based methods. Notably, UNILocPro with timestamps attains performance on par with fully-supervised fingerprinting despite operating without labelled training data. It is also shown that the low-complexity UNILoc can substantially reduce training complexity with marginal performance degradation.
item.dc:creator: Yuhao Zhang, Guangjin Pan, Musa Furkan Keskin, Ossi Kaltiokallio, Mikko Valkama, Henk Wymeersch

item.title: Unsupervised End-to-End Array Calibration for Multi-Target Integrated Sensing and Communication
item.description: arXiv:2604.00806v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we consider end-to-end calibration of an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) base station (BS) under gain-phase and antenna displacement impairments without collecting signals from predefined positions (labeled data). We consider a BS with two impaired uniform linear arrays used for simultaneous multi-target sensing and communication with a user equipment (UE) leveraging orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing signals. The main contribution is the design of a framework that can compensate for the impairments without labeled data and considering coherent receive signals. We harness a differentiable precoder based on the maximum array response in an angular direction at the transmitter and the orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) algorithm at the sensing receiver. We propose an ISAC loss as a combination of sensing and communication losses that provides a trade-off between the two functionalities. We compare two sensing objective alternatives: (i) maximize the maximum response of the angle-delay map of the targets or (ii) minimize the norm of the residual signal at the output of the OMP algorithm after all estimated targets have been removed. The communication objective maximizes the energy of the received signal at the UE. Additionally, our framework leverages an approximation of the channel gradient that avoids the impractical knowledge of the gradient of the channel. Our results show that the proposed method performs closely to using labeled data and knowledge of the channel gradient in terms of sensing position estimation and communication symbol error rate. When comparing the two sensing losses, minimizing the norm of the OMP residual yields significantly better sensing position estimation with slightly increased complexity.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Miguel Mateos-Ramos, Baptiste Chatelier, Luc Le Magoarou, Nir Shlezinger, Henk Wymeersch, Christian H\"ager

item.title: Opportunistic Cooperative Sensing in mmWave ISAC Networks: A Meta-Distribution Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2604.06069v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose an opportunistic cooperative sensing architecture for millimeter-wave (mmWave) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) networks that harvests bistatic echoes from already-active transmissions of neighboring base stations (BSs). Each target is sensed by its nearest BS, while neighboring BSs contribute only when their scheduled beams opportunistically illuminate the target. Cooperation requires neither beam reconfiguration nor dedicated air-interface resources and can leverage existing 5G transport and edge-computing infrastructure for synchronization and local echo processing. Using stochastic geometry, we characterize the sensing meta-distribution for cooperative ISAC, quantifying target-level reliability beyond spatial averages when multiple cooperative echoes are combined, while also analyzing sensing and communication coverage and ergodic rates. Results show that opportunistic cooperation substantially improves average sensing performance and target-level reliability. For instance, at a sensing signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) threshold of 5 dB, increasing the maximum cooperative-cluster size from 1 to 6 raises the percentage of targets whose conditional sensing success probability exceeds 90% by over 55 percentage points. The results further reveal practical design tradeoffs in cluster sizing, BS densification, and sensing-communication energy allocation.
item.dc:creator: Yasser Nabil, Hesham ElSawy, Hossam S. Hassanein

item.title: Set-Theoretic PAPR Reduction in Multi-Antenna Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.15557v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this study, we propose an optimization framework for PAPR reduction in multi-antenna systems with beamforming. Unlike previous techniques, the proposed approach permits full control over the distorted symbol constellation via arbitrary (convex) constraints on the frequency domain symbols, while minimizing the PAPR at each individual transmit antenna. We propose an iterative algorithm based on an extrapolated alternating projection method, which relies on an iterative soft-thresholding subroutine to compute projections onto sublevel sets of the objective function, and we compare its performance to optimal solutions obtained with general-purpose convex solvers.
item.dc:creator: Jochen Fink, Renato L. G. Cavalcante, S{\l}awomir Sta\'nczak

item.title: 20 GHz Longitudinal Surface Acoustic Wave Resonators in 100-nm X-Cut Lithium Niobate on Silicon Carbide
item.description: arXiv:2611.25409v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonators above 15~GHz require a fast acoustic mode that retains strong electromechanical coupling ($k^2$). This work reports longitudinal SAW (L-SAW) resonators designed for high $k^2$ in 100-nm X-cut lithium niobate (LN) on 4H silicon carbide (SiC), operating up to 21.7~GHz and reaching a $k^2$ of 8.1\%, a maximum Bode $Q$ of 70, and a figure of merit (FoM) of 5.7 at 20.24~GHz. In this thin-film waveguide, shrinking the wavelength ($\lambda$) keeps the normalized LN thickness ($h_\mathrm{LN}/\lambda$) large, sustaining both $k^2$ and acoustic confinement. Conversely, increasing $\lambda$ from 292 to 471~nm lowers $h_\mathrm{LN}/\lambda$ from 0.34 to 0.21 and raises the L-SAW phase velocity from 6.32 to 7.05~km/s, within 1.1\% of the 7126-m/s shear-wave velocity of 4H-SiC. As the velocity approaches this limit, more of the acoustic energy spreads into the non-piezoelectric SiC, and $k^2$ falls from its 8.1\% peak at $\lambda = 322$~nm to 1.7\% at $\lambda = 471$~nm. No L-SAW resonance is observed for $\lambda \geq 518$~nm ($h_\mathrm{LN}/\lambda \leq 0.19$), where the mode becomes leaky. Overall, the FoM stays within 5\% of its maximum for $h_\mathrm{LN}/\lambda$ between 0.26 to 0.31, defining a design window for L-SAW resonators in thin LN on SiC at K-band and beyond.
item.dc:creator: Jiajun Huang, Ziqian Yao, Tzu-Hsuan Hsu, Ian Anderson, Joshua Campbell, Ruochen Lu

item.title: A Survey of Advancing Audio Super-Resolution and Bandwidth Extension from Discriminative to Generative Models
item.description: arXiv:2605.16681v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Audio super-resolution (SR), also referred to as bandwidth extension (BWE), aims to reconstruct high-fidelity signals from low-resolution (LR) or band-limited (BL) observations, an inherently ill-posed task due to the ambiguity of missing high-frequency (HF) content. This survey provides a comprehensive overview of the field, with a particular focus on the paradigm shift from discriminative mapping to modern generative modeling. We first review early discriminative deep neural network (DNN) models, which formulate BWE/SR as a deterministic mapping problem and are prone to regression-to-the-mean effects and spectral over-smoothing. We then systematically review generative approaches, including autoregressive (AR) models, variational autoencoders (VAEs), generative adversarial networks (GANs), diffusion and score-based models, flow-based methods, and Schr\"odinger bridges. Across these approaches, we examine key design aspects, including representation domain, architecture, conditioning mechanisms, and trade-offs among reconstruction fidelity, perceptual quality, robustness, and computational efficiency. We further conduct unified experiments on representative discriminative and generative methods to provide controlled empirical evidence for these trade-offs. Furthermore, we discuss emerging directions involving large language models (LLMs) and multimodal foundation models, and highlight open challenges in perceptual evaluation, practical deployment, and real-world generalization. By providing a structured taxonomy and unified perspective, this survey establishes a comprehensive foundation and offers a practical roadmap for advancing BWE/SR from deterministic point estimation toward distribution-aware generative modeling.
item.dc:creator: Ningyuan Yang, Yize Li, Diego A. Cuji, Ryan M. Corey, Pu Zhao, Xue Lin, Andrew C. Singer

item.title: A Deep Zero-Inflated Model of North Atlantic Right Whale Presence To Support Blue Economy Management
item.description: arXiv:2606.14403v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Effective modeling of endangered marine mammal species, such as the North Atlantic Right Whale, is critical for balancing marine conservation with the growing blue economy. Passive acoustic monitoring data collected by autonomous underwater vehicles provide new opportunities for localized marine species detection and oceanographic sensing, but introduce complex statistical challenges such as zero inflation, imperfect detection, and intricate dependence structures. In response, we propose the Deep Zero-Inflated Bernoulli (DeepZIB) model, a deep statistical method which jointly models latent species presence and conditional detection probabilities while learning complex habitat relationships from heterogeneous covariate information. We establish theoretical results on the model's structural properties and conduct simulation experiments to demonstrate its ability to recover underlying parameters and latent presence fields. Application to real-world passive acoustic monitoring data on the North Atlantic Right Whale along the U.S. East Coast demonstrates improved model adequacy and predictive performance in capturing the species' dynamic and spatially varying habitat. We demonstrate DeepZIB's ability to generate high-resolution, spatially and temporally varying presence maps, providing valuable insights for targeted and risk-aware management of blue economy industries, ranging from offshore and marine energy, to fisheries management and maritime transport
item.dc:creator: Jiaxiang Ji, Laura Nazzaro, Ahmed Aziz Ezzat

item.title: Reference-Filter-Driven Transition Probabilities for IMM-Based Satellite Maneuver Detection
item.description: arXiv:2610.11242v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Detecting maneuvers of non-cooperative satellites is essential for space situational awareness. The interacting multiple model (IMM) filter has been applied to detect unannounced maneuvers, but the standard IMM assumes a fixed Markov transition probability matrix (TPM) that must be tuned without knowledge of the maneuver rate of the target. To avoid the tuning, adaptive-TPM approaches update the TPM online from statistics computed inside the IMM. However, the statistics already depend on the TPM through the interaction step, and the dependence forms a feedback loop. The loop itself can raise the maneuver probability in the absence of a maneuver or suppress its rise when a maneuver occurs. In this paper, the TPM is driven by the normalized innovation squared (NIS) of a reference coast filter that is decoupled from the IMM, and the NIS is mapped continuously to the coast-to-maneuver transition probability. The reference-driven IMM (RD-IMM) is evaluated with four space-based optical sensors tracking a geostationary target. In the simulation, the reference filter keeps its sensitivity after small maneuvers, whereas the NIS of the coast sub-filter of the IMM is reduced by the interaction step. RD-IMM detects 1-3 m/s maneuvers, which the fixed-TPM IMM rarely detects, with a false-declaration rate below the false-alarm probability of 0.05 set for the reference filter. In the first hour after the 1-3 m/s maneuvers, RD-IMM also has a lower position error than the compared filters.
item.dc:creator: Euiseok Han, Sangheon Choi, Seung-Hyun Kong
